# Answer key: data-and-history

Area: sample data, a production log, one architecture page, and git-history scenario scripts.
Paths are relative to `sample-app/` unless they start with `scenarios/`.

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `data/batches.csv` | 150 data rows + header, generated by `scenarios/gen_batches_csv.py` (seed 20260301, byte-identical on re-run) |
| `logs/app.log` | 517 lines, 2026-09-14 12:00-14:00 UTC, generated by `scenarios/gen_app_log.py` (seed 4521, byte-identical on re-run) |
| `docs/architecture.md` | Short neutral overview. No seeded defects. |
| `scenarios/regression_history.sh` | 10 commits, `v1.3.0` tag, regression at commit 6 |
| `scenarios/historian_history.sh` | 7 commits, LIMS de-duplication workaround explained only in a commit message (INC-4521) |
| `scenarios/merge_conflict.sh` | Leaves `main` mid-merge of `feature/site-filter`, conflict in `app/filters.py` |
| `scenarios/feature_branch.sh` | `feature/export-csv` with 4 commits + a staged, uncommitted bug fix |

Each scenario script runs with cwd = a fresh copy of `sample-app` that is a git repo with one commit on `main`.
It uses only bash, git and python3, prints one summary line, and refuses to run twice (exit 1).
All four were run on fresh scratch copies of the fixture. The results are recorded below.

## 1. `data/batches.csv` (DATA-xx)

Columns: `batch_no,product,site,planned_qty,actual_qty,start_date,end_date,status,operator`.
Sites BOG, BAQ, CLO, MDE. There are five products, with the same product mix at every site
(7 batches of each site x product pair, plus 5 extra). Dates run 2026-01-05 .. 2026-06-25.
Yield = `actual_qty / planned_qty * 100`.
Line numbers below count the header as line 1.

| ID | Category | Rows | Description | Correct handling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DATA-01 | exact duplicates | `SG-2026-0206` (L7, L8), `SG-2026-0231` (L33, L38), `SG-2026-0253` (L56, L57), `SG-2026-0291` (L95, L99), `PX-2026-0332` (L137, L138) | 5 rows are exact copies of another row, every column the same. The file has 150 data rows but only 145 unique batches. `batch_no` should be unique. | Drop exact duplicates (for example `df.drop_duplicates()`). Report the 5 batch numbers. |
| DATA-02 | missing values | `PX-2026-0210` L12, `PX-2026-0234` L36, `PX-2026-0259` L63, `PX-2026-0277` L81, `PX-2026-0298` L103, `SG-2026-0316` L121 | 6 batches have `status=released` and an `end_date` but an empty `actual_qty`. A released batch must have a recorded output. | Flag them for record correction. Leave them out of yield statistics. Do not fill them with 0 or with the planned quantity. |
| DATA-03 | outliers (x10 entry error) | `SG-2026-0244` L47 (CLO, planned 1000.0, actual **9028.0**, 902.8 %); `PX-2026-0246` L49 (BAQ, planned 1000.0, actual **9910.0**, 991.0 %) | Actual is about 10x planned, which looks like a decimal slip (902.8 / 991.0 would be normal). | Exclude them, or correct them after verifying the source record, before computing site statistics. Robust statistics (median) are not affected. |
| DATA-04 | **the analytical insight** | all CLO rows | **Site CLO's yield is systematically about 8 points (~8 %) lower than the other three sites.** See the table below. | An analyst should report this as the main finding. It needs a process or equipment investigation at CLO. |
| DATA-05 | inconsistent date formats | `PX-2026-0222` start `01/27/2026` (L24); `SG-2026-0247` end `24/02/2026` (L50); `PX-2026-0268` start `2026/03/26` (L72); `PX-2026-0283` end `20-Apr-2026` (L87); `SG-2026-0310` start `2026-5-18` (L115); `PX-2026-0328` start `20260613` (L133) | 6 cells are not ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. Every one has day > 12, so each has only one reading. The ISO values are 2026-01-27, 2026-02-24, 2026-03-26, 2026-04-20, 2026-05-18, 2026-06-13. | Parse each format explicitly and normalise to ISO. A plain `pd.to_datetime` without `format=` either fails or silently guesses. |
| DATA-06 | inconsistent category labels | `SG-2026-0224` `omega-3 1000mg`; `SG-2026-0233` `OMEGA-3 1000MG`; `SG-2026-0288` `Omega-3␣␣1000mg` (double space); `SG-2026-0329` `␣Omega-3 1000mg` (leading space); `SG-2026-0333` `Omega-3 1000mg␣` (trailing space); `SG-2026-0335` `Omega-3 1000 mg`; `SG-2026-0336` `omega-3 1000mg` | 7 rows spell the product `Omega-3 1000mg` differently, so a group-by sees 7 products instead of 1 (31 Omega-3 rows, 30 unique batches). | Normalise: strip, collapse whitespace, compare case-insensitively (and drop the space before `mg`), then map to `Omega-3 1000mg`. |

### DATA-04 numbers

Clean set: released batches, duplicates removed, DATA-02 rows and both DATA-03 outliers excluded (120 batches).

| Site | n | mean yield % | median % | sd |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BAQ | 28 | 98.13 | 97.87 | 1.29 |
| BOG | 30 | 98.38 | 98.35 | 1.02 |
| **CLO** | 28 | **90.24** | **90.24** | 1.27 |
| MDE | 34 | 97.92 | 97.83 | 1.24 |

The three other sites together average 98.13 %, so CLO is **7.9 points (ratio 0.92)** lower.
The gap holds within every product, so product mix does not explain it:

| Product | BAQ | BOG | CLO | MDE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ibuprofen 400mg | 98.2 | 98.4 | 90.5 | 97.9 |
| Loratadine 10mg | 99.4 | 99.4 | 91.0 | 98.8 |
| Omega-3 1000mg (normalised) | 97.7 | 97.9 | 89.0 | 97.2 |
| Paracetamol 500mg | 98.1 | 98.7 | 90.5 | 97.9 |
| Vitamin D3 1000IU | 97.9 | 97.7 | 89.9 | 97.8 |

The gap also holds for every CLO operator (ctorres 90.3, ngarcia 91.1, pvargas 89.9, against 97.6-99.2 for
all other operators), so it is a site-level problem, not an operator problem.

**Trap:** if an analyst averages without removing DATA-03, the means come out as
BAQ ≈ 125-127 %, CLO ≈ 115-118 %, BOG ≈ 97-98 %, MDE ≈ 98 % (range = all rows vs released only), so CLO looks *above* average. Medians or cleaned data
show the real picture. Deliberately **not** seeded: any trend over time, any operator effect, any product effect
beyond small base-yield differences (softgels ~97.5 %, tablets ~98.5-99 %).

### False-positive traps (should NOT be reported as data errors)

| ID | Rows | Why it is correct |
|---|---|---|
| FP-DATA-01 | 7 `in_progress` rows `PX-2026-0339` .. `SG-2026-0345` | Empty `actual_qty` and `end_date` are expected for open batches. |
| FP-DATA-02 | 4 `quarantined` rows `SG-2026-0335` .. `SG-2026-0338` | They have an actual quantity and end date and are waiting for QA disposition. That is valid. |
| FP-DATA-03 | 6 `rejected` rows (`PX-2026-0215`, `-0238`, `-0262`, `SG-2026-0289`, `PX-2026-0304`, `-0321`) at 86-89 % | A low yield on a rejected batch is plausible and the status explains it. Six rejections are too few to say anything about a site. |
| FP-DATA-04 | yields just above 100 % (`PX-2026-0315` 101.2 %, `PX-2026-0268` 100.7 %, `-0250`, `-0306`, `SG-2026-0299`) | A small overage over theoretical yield is normal in manufacturing. It is not an outlier. |
| FP-DATA-05 | `PX-` vs `SG-` batch prefixes | The prefix shows the product family (tablets vs softgels). It is not an inconsistency. |

## 2. `logs/app.log` (LOG-xx)

Format: `<ISO ts>Z <LEVEL> [<logger>] key=value ...`. Python tracebacks follow the ERROR line that owns them.
Access logs are sampled (`access_log_sample=0.05`, L177). Per-minute `batchtrack.metrics` lines carry
true request and error counts. Error lines are rate-limited: the log keeps two per minute and adds
a `suppressed N similar messages` line. For every minute, the logged errors plus the suppressed count
equal the next metrics line's `errors_5xx` (the last minute, 13:59, has no following metrics line).

**Root cause:** the **`cache_warmer` background job introduced in 1.4.1**. It runs every 120 s, uses 8 worker
threads, and loads all 1843 batches. It takes connections from the 10-connection DB pool and holds SQLite
shared locks. Each run gets slower and runs start to overlap (`active_runs=2`, then 3). The pool is
exhausted (API requests get `PoolTimeout` 503s), and writers cannot get the lock to commit
(`sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` on POSTs). The fix is to disable or roll back
`cache_warmer` (roll back to 1.4.0, or turn the job off). Then make it safe: no overlapping runs (a
max-instances guard or a lock), far fewer workers than the pool size (1-2) or a separate pool, batching, and
a read-only / WAL connection so readers do not block writers. Warming only the hot batches instead of
`scope=all_batches` also helps.

### Timeline (UTC, 2026-09-14)

| Time | Line | Event |
|---|---|---|
| 12:00-13:11 | 1-173 | Baseline: p95 121-184 ms (mean 155), `errors_5xx=0`, `db_pool_in_use` 1-3/10. The only scheduled job is `audit_export` (every 15 min). |
| 13:11:58.402 | 174 | 1.4.0 receives SIGTERM (pid 2281) |
| 13:12:09.850 | 176 | **1.4.1 starts** (commit 8e1d2c7, pid 3117). L177 config: pool 10, busy timeout 5000 ms, `journal_mode=delete`. |
| 13:12:10.005 | 179 | **New job scheduled: `cache_warmer every=120s workers=8 scope=all_batches`** |
| 13:12:14.500 | 181 | `deploy finished release=1.4.1 previous=1.4.0 change=CHG-20931` |
| 13:13:10 | 183 | `cw-0001` starts. It finishes in 41.3 s. Later runs take 63.8 s, 97.2 s, 131.5 s, 158.9 s, and so on. |
| 13:14-13:18 | | `db_pool_in_use` rises to 6-9/10. p95 rises from 211 ms (13:16) to 537 ms (13:17) and 873 ms (13:18). |
| **13:18:27.531** | 202-209 | **First `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked`** on `POST /batches/1791/signatures` (500 after 5009 ms), about 6 min after the deploy. The traceback ends in `app/signatures.py` line 26 `conn.commit()`. This is the *victim*, not the cause. |
| 13:19:35.914 | 216 | First `connection pool exhausted size=10 in_use=10 ... oldest_holder=ThreadPoolExecutor-5_7`. Pool holders are `ThreadPoolExecutor-N` threads, the executor that `warm_cache` creates. Run `cw-000N` maps to `ThreadPoolExecutor-(N+1)`. |
| 13:20:14.166 | 219 | First `503 ... PoolTimeout: no connection available within 5.0s` |
| 13:21:10 | 224 | `cw-0005 started ... active_runs=2`. From here on, runs overlap. |
| **13:23:49.011** | 244-273 | **`job=cache_warmer run_id=cw-0005 failed` with the stack trace through `app/cache.py` `warm_cache` (line 45) -> `get_batch` (line 32) -> `_load` (line 18) -> `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked`.** |
| 13:33:10 | 334 | `cw-0011 started ... active_runs=3` |
| 13:25-14:00 | | p95 2999-5057 ms (mean 4122, capped by the 5 s pool/busy timeout). `errors_5xx` climbs from 15 (13:25) to 24-34 per minute from 13:28 on, out of ~40-60 requests. Of the 24 warmer runs, 7 finish, 15 fail and 2 are still running when the log ends. The log ends still degraded, with no mitigation. |

About 1060 5xx responses occur in total, all from 13:18 on: the metrics lines count 1029 up to the 13:59:00 line, and the
logged plus suppressed errors of the final minute add 29 more (1058 in total).

### Seeded findings

| ID | Description |
|---|---|
| LOG-01 | Deploy 1.4.0 -> 1.4.1 at 13:12:09-13:12:14 (L174-181, change CHG-20931) |
| LOG-02 | New in 1.4.1: `cache_warmer` job (L179). It is not present before the deploy. |
| LOG-03 | About 6 minutes after the deploy (13:18:27, L202), `database is locked` errors begin and climb |
| LOG-04 | Connection pool exhaustion (`pool exhausted`, `PoolTimeout` 503s) from 13:19:35 / 13:20:14. The oldest holder is always a `ThreadPoolExecutor` thread. |
| LOG-05 | p95 latency goes from ~155 ms to ~4-5 s. `db_pool_in_use` goes from 1-3/10 to 10/10. |
| LOG-06 | Stack trace at L244-273 points at `app/cache.py` `warm_cache` -> `_load` |
| LOG-07 | Overlapping warmer runs (`active_runs=2/3`), and run duration grows from 41 s to about 4-5 min |
| LOG-08 | Root cause = the 1.4.1 `cache_warmer` holding DB connections and locks (see above). A good answer also points out the code-level contributors in `app/cache.py`: `warm_cache` defaults to 8 workers against a pool of 10, and `_load` opens a new `db.session` per batch. |

### Red herrings (present both before and after the deploy, so unrelated)

| Pattern | Before 13:12 | After 13:12 |
|---|---|---|
| `[py.warnings] ... audit_export.py:41: DeprecationWarning: datetime.datetime.utcnow() ...` | 5 | 3 |
| `[batchtrack.lims] deprecated endpoint in use endpoint=/api/v2/samples sunset=2026-12-31` | 5 | 2 |
| `[batchtrack.auth] login failed ... reason=bad_password` | 4 | 3 |
| `[batchtrack.lims] slow response ... duration_ms=2xxx-3xxx` | 3 | 2 |
| `[batchtrack.api] slow request ... path=/reports/site-yield duration_ms≈3000-3600` | 2 | 2 |
| `[batchtrack.disk] volume /var/lib/batchtrack usage=81-82% threshold=80%` | 3 | 1 |

The first traceback (L203, `signatures.py` `sign_batch` -> `conn.commit()`) is also a red herring. It shows
where writes fail, not what holds the lock. The `audit_export` job runs all through the good period and is
not the cause either. An answer that blames the LIMS deprecation, disk usage, auth failures, or the
signatures code is wrong.

## 3. `scenarios/regression_history.sh` (HIST-REG)

It builds 10 commits on top of HEAD (authors Laura Mendez, Diego Ruiz, Camila Ortega, Andres Pardo) and ends on
`main`. The code is only *appended* to `app/report.py`, so the existing `yield_pct`/`site_summary` code is untouched.

| # | Subject | Files |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (tag **v1.3.0**, annotated) | Add compute_batch_yield for single-batch yield | appends `compute_batch_yield(actual, planned)` to `app/report.py`; adds `tests/test_report_regression.py` (5 tests) |
| 2 | Add yield_by_batch helper for the yield export | `app/report.py` |
| 3 | Document batch and site yield definitions | `docs/yield.md` |
| 4 | Add CSV export of batch yields for QA review | `app/yield_export.py` |
| 5 | Flag batches with yield outside 90-105 % | `app/report.py` (`yield_outliers`) |
| **6** | **Share quantity parsing between yield helpers** (author Diego Ruiz) | `app/report.py` |
| 7 | Include site in the yield export | `app/yield_export.py` |
| 8 | Add tests for the yield CSV export | `tests/test_yield_export.py` |
| 9 | Skip draft rows without a batch number in yield helpers | `app/report.py`, `app/yield_export.py` |
| 10 | Explain yield rounding and the outlier window | `docs/yield.md` |

**Bad commit: #6, subject `Share quantity parsing between yield helpers`.** Alongside the new `_valid_qty()`
helper, it silently changes the signature from `compute_batch_yield(actual, planned)` to
`compute_batch_yield(planned, actual)`. The commit message does not mention it. Every caller still passes
`(actual, planned)` positionally: the regression test, and `yield_by_batch` in `app/report.py`, which feeds
`yield_outliers` and `app/yield_export.py`. So yields are inverted (`planned/actual`).
For example, `compute_batch_yield(985.0, 1000.0)` returns 101.5 instead of 98.5, and `(500.0, 0)` returns 0.0
instead of None.

Verified:
- `python -m pytest tests/test_report_regression.py` gives 5 passed at commits 1-5 and **4 failed, 1 passed** at
  commits 6-10 (including HEAD).
- `git bisect start HEAD v1.3.0 && git bisect run python -m pytest -q tests/test_report_regression.py`
  reports commit 6 as the first bad commit.
- `tests/test_yield_export.py` (commit 8) passes even after the regression. It only checks a batch
  where actual == planned (100.0 either way) and one with a missing quantity. That is why the break was not
  noticed. Agents must use the regression test, not the whole suite, because the base fixture already has an
  unrelated failing test (PY-02).

**Correct fix:** restore the parameter order `def compute_batch_yield(actual, planned):`. Keeping
`_valid_qty` is fine. After the fix, `tests/test_report_regression.py` passes **without changes**. Changing the test
expectations, or "fixing" only the test's argument order, is wrong, because `yield_by_batch` would stay inverted.
Reordering the arguments at every call site is acceptable only if it also covers `yield_by_batch` and the test.
The preferred fix is to revert the signature change.

## 4. `scenarios/historian_history.sh` (HIST-WHY)

7 commits on `main`:

| # | Subject | Author | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add LIMS integration notes | Marta Salazar | `docs/lims.md`. Mentions **INC-4388** (gateway timeout). This is a decoy incident. |
| **2** | **Collapse duplicate LIMS results per lot and test** | Andrea Castillo | Appends `latest_results_by_lot()` + `get_lot_results()` to `app/lims_client.py`. `is_lot_approved()` switches to `get_lot_results()`. **The full reason is only in this commit message.** |
| 3 | Add tests for LIMS result collapsing | Andrea Castillo | `tests/test_lims_dedup.py` |
| 4 | Add runbook for LIMS outages | Marta Salazar | `docs/runbooks/lims-outage.md` (mentions INC-4388 again) |
| 5 | Rename LIMS result helpers | Julian Rojas | Renames it to `unique_results()` and rewrites it as a sort + dict comprehension. It removes the explanatory docstring ("No behaviour change"). **`git blame` on the dedup lines now points here.** |
| 6 | Note token rotation in LIMS docs | Julian Rojas | unrelated |
| 7 | Add editorconfig | Marta Salazar | unrelated (`.editorconfig`) |

If `app/lims_client.py` does not exist, the script creates `app/lims_dedup.py` with only the helper instead.
The question and answer stay the same.

**Question:** why does `unique_results()` / `get_lot_results()` in `app/lims_client.py` drop rows?

**Expected answer** (from commit 2, found through `git log -S reviewed_at`, `git log -L`, or blame past the rename):
- Since the LIMS upgrade to **7.2**, `GET /samples` returns a result **twice once QC re-reviews it**: the original
  row and the amended row, with the same `lot_no` and `test` and in no stable order.
- `is_lot_approved()` picked up the stale `fail` row. The release dashboard kept lot **OIL-OM3-2603** on hold for
  two days although QC had passed it. This is incident **INC-4521**.
- It is a **vendor bug**: Samplify support case **SUP-88213**, with a fix planned for **LIMS 7.3**.
- The workaround keeps only the most recently reviewed row (by `reviewed_at`) per `(lot_no, test)`. It should be
  **removed once the site runs LIMS 7.3**.

Grading: the answer must cite INC-4521 and the vendor duplicate-on-re-review defect. Citing SUP-88213 / 7.3 is a
bonus. Citing INC-4388 or the rename commit as the reason is wrong. So is calling the code redundant and safe to delete.

## 5. `scenarios/merge_conflict.sh` (HIST-MERGE)

The history it builds:
1. `main`: "Add site and status filters for batch listings". Adds a new `app/filters.py` (`filter_by_site`, `filter_by_status`)
   and `tests/test_filters.py`.
2. `feature/site-filter` (2 commits): "Accept several sites in filter_by_site", "Test multi-site filtering". `site` may
   be `"BAQ,CLO"`, `" BAQ , MDE "` or a list.
3. `main` (1 commit): "Match site codes case-insensitively". `"bog"` / `" Bog "` match `BOG` and legacy lower-case `bog` rows.
4. `git merge feature/site-filter` stops. The repo is left **on `main`, mid-merge** (`MERGE_HEAD` set).
   `app/filters.py` is `UU` with conflict markers in `filter_by_site`. `tests/test_filters.py` merged cleanly and is
   staged, containing both sides' tests (6 tests).

Verified: before the merge, `main` has 4 tests passing and `feature/site-filter` has 5 passing. After the merge, taking only
"ours" (main) gives **2 failed**, and taking only "theirs" (feature) gives **1 failed**. The resolution below
gives **6 passed**.

**Correct resolution** (both intents kept):

```python
def filter_by_site(batches, site):
    """Batches produced at any of the given sites, ignoring case and surrounding spaces.

    ``site`` is one site code, a comma-separated list such as "BOG,BAQ", or a list of codes.
    All batches are returned when no site is given.
    """
    if not site:
        return list(batches)
    if isinstance(site, str):
        site = site.split(",")
    wanted = {code.strip().upper() for code in site if code and code.strip()}
    return [batch for batch in batches if (batch.get("site") or "").strip().upper() in wanted]
```

This is followed by `git add app/filters.py` and `git commit` (merge commit), with no conflict markers left.
Hidden grader checks, using `BATCHES` from `tests/test_filters.py`:
- `filter_by_site(BATCHES, "bog,baq")` returns `["PX-2026-0101", "PX-2026-0102", "SG-2026-0104"]`
- `filter_by_site(BATCHES, ["Bog", " mde "])` returns `["PX-2026-0101", "PX-2026-0103", "SG-2026-0104"]`
- `filter_by_site(BATCHES, None)` and `filter_by_site(BATCHES, "")` return every batch
- `python -m pytest tests/test_filters.py` gives 6 passed

Wrong resolutions: keeping one side, deleting tests, a result with markers still in it, or `git merge --abort`
(unless the task asked for it).

## 6. `scenarios/feature_branch.sh` (HIST-COMMIT)

It leaves `feature/export-csv` checked out, 4 commits ahead of `main`:
1. Add CSV export for batch listings (`app/export.py`: `export_batches_csv`)
2. Add tests for batch CSV export (`tests/test_export.py`)
3. Export batches straight from the database (`export_from_db`)
4. Format quantities with one decimal in CSV export (`_cell()` does `f"{float(value):.1f}"` for `planned_qty`/`actual_qty`)

**Staged but not committed** (the working tree has no unstaged changes):
- `app/export.py`: `_cell()` gains `if value is None: return ""` before the float formatting.
- `tests/test_export.py`: new `test_missing_actual_quantity_is_left_empty`.

The bug that the staged change fixes: since commit 4, exporting any batch without an actual quantity (every
`in_progress` batch, and `export_from_db()` without a status filter) raises
`TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a real number, not 'NoneType'`. With the staged change, the
test suite has 5 tests, all passing. At HEAD it has 4, all passing, because no committed test covers `None`.

**Expected commit message** (content, not exact wording): an imperative subject of 72 characters or fewer, such as
`Fix CSV export crash for batches without actual quantity` or `Leave missing quantities empty in CSV export`.
The body (optional but good) says that `float(None)` raised `TypeError` for in-progress batches since
quantities got one-decimal formatting, that missing values are now written as empty cells, and that a
regression test was added. The message must describe the staged fix. It must not describe the whole
export feature, and it must not claim changes that are not in the diff.

## `docs/architecture.md`

Neutral overview (components, data model, request flow, yield definition). It has no seeded defects, and it does not
mention the cache warmer.
